sections.title: Scores are not probabilities yet
paragraphs: A neuron can emit a raw score for each option: cat, dog, bird or the next {{token}} in a sentence. Those scores are sometimes called logits. They are not probabilities until you reshape them.
{{softmax}} turns a list of scores into a list of positive numbers that add up to one. The largest score becomes the largest share; smaller scores keep a smaller share.

Why bother? Training and sampling need a distribution. Cross-entropy {{loss}} compares a probability vector to a one-hot {{target}}. Next-token generation samples from a distribution over the vocabulary.
Elementwise {{activation}}s like {{sigmoid}} or {{relu}} act on one number at a time. {{softmax}} looks at the whole vector so options compete.
This is inside-model maths: how the network turns internal scores into a {{prediction}} distribution before anyone writes a product {{prompt}}.
bullets: Raw scores: unbounded comparisons between options.
{{softmax}}: map scores to probabilities that sum to 1.
Use case: multi-class labels and next-{{token}} choice.

check.prompt: Three scores become 0.7, 0.2 and 0.1 after {{softmax}}. What must be true?
check.answer: They are probabilities that add to one
choices: They are probabilities that add to one
Softmax always outputs exactly two numbers
The smallest score always becomes probability 1
check.explanation: {{softmax}} outputs a distribution: each entry is at least zero and the entries sum to one. That is what makes them usable as probabilities for a {{prediction}}.

sections.title: Sharpening and flattening the distribution
paragraphs: If one score is much larger than the others, {{softmax}} puts almost all mass on that option. The {{prediction}} looks confident.
If scores are close, the distribution stays flatter. Many options keep meaningful probability.
Dividing scores by a positive temperature-like constant before {{softmax}} changes sharpness. Lower values peak harder; higher values flatten. That maths lives inside the probability step.

Later, outside the model, product knobs named {{temperature}} reuse the same idea when sampling text. Do not confuse the layers: the formula is inside; the API dial is an outside control you will lock for fair evals.
Click each case. The optional Softmax lab lets you drag three scores and watch the bars reshape.

reveals.reveal: Almost all probability lands on the first option. The distribution is sharp.
Nearly uniform probabilities. The model is undecided among the three.

reveals.prompt: You need a crisp class {{prediction}} for training.
reveals.reveal: A peaked distribution matches a clear {{target}} class. Flat distributions fight one-hot labels.

check.prompt: A teammate says {{temperature}} on an API is the same thing as a {{weights}} matrix. What is the clearer split?
check.answer: Softmax maths is inside; sampling dials are outside controls
choices: Softmax maths is inside; sampling dials are outside controls
Temperature rewrites every weight in the network
Softmax only exists in decision trees
API temperature trains new embeddings from scratch
check.explanation: {{softmax}} (and score scaling) is part of turning logits into probabilities inside the model. Product {{temperature}} knobs change sampling behavior outside when you generate text.

sections.title: Into the neural network lab
paragraphs: You now have the chain for a classifier-style head: weighted sums, {{activation}}s in hidden layers, then often {{softmax}} on the final scores.
The Neural network lab keeps some heads simple so you can focus on {{loss}} falling. Still, when you see multi-class language later, remember the distribution view.
Honesty: stable {{softmax}} subtracts the max score before exp to avoid overflow. Libraries do that for you; the lab can show the probabilities without forcing you to type the formula.

check.prompt: In a short phrase, what does {{softmax}} add on top of raw scores?
accept: a distribution over classes or tokens
check.explanation: {{softmax}} converts competing scores into a {{prediction}} distribution. That is the inside step before you treat outputs as class chances or next-{{token}} chances.

recapQuestions.prompt: Why use {{softmax}} instead of reading raw scores as final answers?
recapQuestions.answer: You need probabilities that compete and sum to one
choices: You need probabilities that compete and sum to one
Softmax deletes the need for any training data
Raw scores are already guaranteed to be between 0 and 1
Softmax only formats JSON for judges
recapQuestions.explanation: Training losses and sampling need a proper distribution. {{softmax}} is the standard inside map from logits to probabilities.

recapQuestions.prompt: Complete: elementwise {{relu}} acts on one unit; {{softmax}}…
recapQuestions.answer: Looks at the whole score vector at once
accept: lets options compete in one step
recapQuestions.explanation: {{softmax}} is a vector {{activation}}: every option's probability depends on every score, not on a single number in isolation.
